newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ZWACK SAYS H1 SALES, PROFITS UP.
newsitem.headline: ZWACK SAYS H1 SALES, PROFITS UP.

text.p: Hungarian alcoholic beverages producer Zwack Unicum Rt reported rising profits and sales for the first half of 1997, and said that some parts of the legal spirit market has begun to increase.

"The significant trend of a decreasing legal spirit market that started in 1995, is continuing in 1997," Zwack said in its earnings report on Wednesday. "However, some segments of spirit market started to grow in the last six months."

Zwack reported its consolidated IAS operating profits rising to 444 million forints in the first six months of 1997 from 378 million in the first six months of 1996, while its profit on ordinary activities before tax grew to 281 million from 202 million.
Illegal alcohol sales have had a negative impact on Zwack's domestic sales in recent years.

Zwack continued to upgrade its product portfolio, it said, adding that its new apricot brandy was launched in May as the first pure distillate from the renewed distillery in Kecskemet, central-east Hungary.
The company said earlier this year it completed an over 500 million forint investment in Kecskemet where it has established what it claimed was central Europe's most modern fruit spirits distillery.
